I will still lean on the wheat-maize rotation for most of my land, because I have 40 mu and only one person in the house, so I cannot put too much land into cotton. Cotton brings cash, but it eats labor and pesticide money, and if I spread myself too thin, I will lose on management. What I do is start from what has worked here: winter wheat on the main land, summer maize right after wheat, and only a small block of cotton on the side. With well irrigation, I do not dare save too much on fertilizer. If I am unsure, I would rather put a little extra nitrogen than watch the crop go yellow. For wheat, I will use improved seed and feed it a bit heavier, because wheat here answers well to water and fertilizer. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed and keep the stand strong after wheat harvest, usually with less tillage so I can move fast. For cotton, I will keep only 5 mu, use better seed, more potassium than grain crops, and spray more times because insects on cotton are never light. I also watch what the good farmers around me do. Nobody around me with irrigated land and decent yields is farming these crops on empty fertilizer now. I will spend where yield is protected first, then control pesticide and labor tightly so the whole year still balances.
